target.value: CSOs with increased capacities to design and implement effective and principled humanitarian response CSOs with increased voice to influence the humanitarian agenda in their country

actual.value:
Advocacy initiatives took place in the two countries as well as at global level together with other civil society actors including local actors and partners. Several briefs on the Syrian and Lebanon contexts were developed including two studies on migration and returns amongst Syrian refugees and vulnerable Lebanese in Lebanon and menstrual hygiene management in Syria respectively. Online information sharing mechanism for refugees and IDPs was also established. The activities were reduced mainly due to COVID-19 restrictions which did not allow for physical meetings and travels, but also the significant shocks during the period and increased complexity of providing life-saving activities impacted this objective.
Capacity development took place as trainings, peer to peer learning and co-implementation. In Syria it also included eight local civil society organizations who are not formal partners with Oxfam.

actual.value:
Lebanon: 4.629 individuals gained access to safe and adequate water and dislodging services including water tanks and four rounds of desludging.
Syria: In Syria pipelines and spot rehabilitation of Jawar Alward water pumping station provided safe drinking water to more than 8.500 people in Tal Al-Daman and Jabal Saman Areas.
